$comment: What AgentDeck verifies, where, and what it does not. Rendered as the 'What we verify' tab of the GitHub Pages Build Health report (scripts/generate-html-report.py). Gated by scripts/__tests__/verification-catalog.test.ts: every workflow must be listed, every path must exist, and every test file must match a domain (domains are ordered; the first match wins). Edit this file in the same commit as a new gate, workflow or test area. Gate fields: `blocking` means a failure turns its workflow red; `required` means master branch protection lists the gate's check, so GitHub refuses the merge while it fails. Branch protection is a repository setting that CI cannot read, so `merge_policy.as_of` records when `required` was last checked against it.

merge_policy.summary: Branch protection on master requires one status check, ESP32 Sim Compile. Every other gate turns a pull request red when it fails but does not stop GitHub from merging it.

levels.unit: One module in isolation; collaborators faked.
levels.contract: A wire format, generated mirror or SSOT table compared against its canonical source. Catches drift, not behaviour.
levels.integration: Several real modules together in one process (real sockets on ephemeral loopback ports, real files in a temp dir).
levels.e2e: The shipped entry point started as a separate process and driven only through its public interfaces.
levels.compile: Source builds for the target; nothing executes.
levels.static: Lint, type check, link or token checks over source text.
levels.hardware: Runs against a connected physical device.
levels.release: Packaging, signing and store-submission checks on a release tag.

gates.name: TypeScript suite (Vitest) + coverage floor
gates.trigger: Every PR and push to master
proves: bridge, shared, hooks, plugin, plugin-ulanzi, setup and scripts behave as their tests specify (the domain table below counts them)
line/function/branch/statement coverage of bridge, shared, plugin and hooks stays above the floor in vitest.config.ts
generated Swift/Kotlin/C++ mirrors match their TypeScript source of truth (contract tests)
does_not_prove: anything about native apps, firmware or real devices
macOS-only halves (Swift toolchain, launchd) — those cases are marked skipped on Linux and appear as skipped in this report

gates.name: Daemon hub end-to-end
gates.trigger: Every PR and push to master
proves: the real agentdeck daemon start process boots in an empty HOME and answers /health
Claude hook events posted to /hooks/* drive the WebSocket state stream (idle → processing → idle)
the exact hook shell snippet the installer writes finds the daemon through daemon.json and delivers events
PreToolUse and Stop hooks answer immediately when no device can approve, so Claude never stalls
the timeline is persisted to timeline.json and replayed to a new client after a restart
SIGTERM shuts the daemon down on its own and withdraws daemon.json
loopback posture: the port is closed on the host's LAN address
does_not_prove: a real Claude/Codex process (events are posted with the documented payload shape)
LAN pairing and default-deny from another machine (every same-host address is trusted by design; the gate itself is unit-tested in http-auth-gate.test.ts)
device modules (all disabled with --local)

gates.name: Sandboxed Swift Codex live acceptance
gates.where: Maintainer Mac running the signed sandboxed app
gates.trigger: Opt-in after deploying the Swift app
proves: A verified sandboxed Swift process accepts Codex lifecycle HTTP events and broadcasts matching WebSocket roster states
Late OTel cannot override hook ownership, prevent real-time terminal expiry, or resurrect an expired hook row
OTel-only and notify-plus-OTel fallback and turn-ID guards remain functional
does_not_prove: Real Codex CLI emission, interactive trust, or installer configuration preservation (events are synthetic)
App Store distribution, Kiro folder consent/revocation, OpenCode SSE reconnect, or physical display pixels
Unattended hosted CI: requires an explicitly selected running Mac app and leaves labeled synthetic timeline entries

gates.name: Build + type check + version and protocol drift
gates.trigger: Every PR and push to master
gates.command: pnpm verify-version && pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm generate-protocol (no diff)
proves: every workspace package compiles under strict TypeScript
target versions agree with the repository compatibility major
generated protocol types (Swift, Kotlin, JSON Schema) are committed in sync with shared/src/protocol.ts
does_not_prove: runtime behaviour

gates.name: Windows native runtime (Node 22 / 24 / 26)
gates.trigger: Every PR and push to master
gates.command: node bridge/dist/cli.js diag native --json && vitest run <8 Windows-sensitive files>
proves: better-sqlite3 opens under each supported Node ABI on Windows
hook installer, observer, state machine and daemon launcher/supervisor tests pass on Windows paths and shells
does_not_prove: the Scheduled Task autostart on a real login session
the Stream Deck app on Windows

gates.name: Design system, docs and mirror gates
gates.trigger: Every PR and push to master
gates.command: verify-tokens-sync.py, design-system:check, docs:check, devlog:check, surface/GNB/spec-card parity, design/lint.sh
proves: colour/type tokens are identical across CSS, JS, TS, Swift, Kotlin and C++ mirrors
every Markdown link and anchor resolves; every docs/ file is cataloged or excluded with a reason
the AGENTS.md chain (root + nested) stays under Codex's 32 KiB project_doc_max_bytes and no CLAUDE.md-family file shadows it inside the checkout
the development log aggregates match their entries
does_not_prove: how anything looks on a device

gates.name: Android JUnit + Robolectric
proves: the Android app compiles
protocol parsing, timeline store and state logic behave as specified on the JVM
does_not_prove: Compose UI on a device or e-ink panel (there are no instrumented tests)

gates.name: Apple XCTest (macOS) + iOS build
gates.trigger: PRs and pushes touching apple/**, shared/** or generated/protocol/**
gates.command: xcodebuild test -scheme AgentDeck_macOS; xcodebuild build -scheme AgentDeck_iOS; validate-appstore-submission.sh
proves: the macOS app and its in-process Swift daemon build and pass XCTest
the iOS app builds unsigned
App Store metadata, screenshots and privacy manifest are within submission limits
does_not_prove: UI flows (there is no UI-test target)
behaviour on a signed build with real TCC grants

gates.name: ESP32 firmware host build
proves: the real esp32/src render trees compile for the native simulator
does_not_prove: the Xtensa build, flashing, or behaviour on a board

gates.name: This report
gates.command: vitest --coverage, pnpm test:e2e, gradlew testDebugUnitTest, then generate-html-report.py
proves: re-runs the Vitest, E2E and Android suites on the merged master commit and publishes every result
does_not_prove: Apple, hardware or release gates — those run in their own workflows and are linked, not re-run here

gates.name: ESP32 Robot Framework (flash, boot, serial protocol, performance)
gates.trigger: Manually before an ESP32 firmware release
proves: the firmware flashes, boots, parses the serial JSON protocol and meets heap/latency budgets on real boards
does_not_prove: anything in GitHub CI — no hosted runner has the boards, so this page shows it as not run

gates.name: Build-and-deploy smoke on real devices
gates.where: maintainer lab (Mac, phones, e-ink readers, Stream Deck, ESP32)
proves: the built artifacts install and connect to a daemon on the maintainer's hardware
does_not_prove: repeatability — results are not recorded here

gates.name: npm publish
gates.command: build, pnpm test, publish, verify packages visible on the registry
proves: the published packages were built from a green test run and are visible on npm
does_not_prove: a fresh npx @agentdeck/setup install on a clean machine

gates.name: App Store / TestFlight upload
proves: the signed archive satisfies the App Store self-containment invariants before upload
does_not_prove: runs no XCTest itself — relies on apple-test.yml having passed on master

gates.name: Android APK / Play upload
gates.command: assembleSideload, apksigner verify, bundle, Play internal track
proves: the release APK is signed with the release key
does_not_prove: runs no tests itself — relies on android-test.yml having passed on master

gates.name: ESP32 firmware release
gates.command: pio run per board, merge factory image, checksums, manifest
proves: every supported board's firmware builds and ships with a checksummed manifest
does_not_prove: boot on hardware (see the Robot suites)

gates.name: Stream Deck plugin package
proves: the .streamDeckPlugin bundle packages
does_not_prove: the DRM-processed Marketplace build (verified manually through Elgato's review loop)

gates.name: Ulanzi plugin package
proves: the Ulanzi plugin bundle packages with its WASM renderer and fonts
does_not_prove: behaviour inside Ulanzi Studio (manual, plugin-ulanzi/VERIFY.md)

not_a_gate..github/workflows/asc-certificates.yml: Manual App Store Connect certificate maintenance; verifies nothing about the product.

not_verified.what: A real Claude Code / Codex / OpenCode process driving the daemon
not_verified.why: Needs an authenticated agent CLI and spends model tokens on every run.
not_verified.instead: The daemon E2E posts the documented hook payloads through the installed snippet; parsers are covered by recorded-output unit tests.

not_verified.what: LAN default-deny against a second machine
not_verified.why: Every address of the host itself is trusted by design, so a single CI runner cannot be a LAN peer.
not_verified.instead: The access gate is a pure function with a full truth-table test (http-auth-gate.test.ts); the E2E checks the loopback bind.

not_verified.what: Stream Deck, Ulanzi, Android, iOS and macOS user interfaces
not_verified.why: No UI-test or instrumented-test targets exist; the host apps (Stream Deck, Ulanzi Studio) cannot run in CI.
not_verified.instead: Renderer snapshot tests, layout-engine tests and manual device deploys.

not_verified.what: Firmware behaviour on ESP32 boards, Pixoo, Timebox, iDotMatrix, TC001
not_verified.instead: Host-simulator compile gate, protocol unit tests, and the lab Robot suites before firmware releases.

not_verified.what: macOS privacy prompts (Automation, Accessibility, Screen Recording, Local Network, Bluetooth, firewall)
not_verified.why: They belong to a signed app on a real user session.
not_verified.instead: scripts/macos-preflight.sh checks the grants before a lab run and stops with the exact System Settings path instead of hanging on a dialog.

domains.name: LAN security & pairing
domains.question: Is the LAN surface default-deny, and does pairing hand out credentials only with the operator's consent?

domains.name: End-to-end (real processes)
domains.question: Does the shipped daemon work when started and driven from outside?

domains.name: Timeline
domains.question: Is every turn, task and approval recorded once, attributed to the right session, and kept across restarts?

domains.name: Usage & quota
domains.question: Are Claude, Codex and Z.ai quota windows read, relayed and aged correctly?

domains.name: Daemon lifecycle & CLI
domains.question: Does exactly one daemon own the port, start, upgrade, restart and hand over cleanly on every OS?

domains.name: Agent observation & hooks
domains.question: Are Claude, Codex, OpenCode, Kiro, Antigravity and Hermes sessions seen, attributed and gated correctly from their hooks and transcripts?

domains.name: Managed sessions & terminal parsing
domains.question: Does agentdeck claude|codex read the terminal correctly and route commands to the right PTY?

domains.name: State machine & hub protocol
domains.question: Do agent states transition correctly and reach every client in the documented wire shape?

domains.name: APME evaluation
domains.question: Are turns and tasks segmented, judged and scored correctly, and does the recommender rank models honestly?

domains.name: OpenClaw Gateway
domains.question: Does the Gateway proxy stay subscribed, attribute runs and approvals, and report its health truthfully?

domains.name: Devices & display surfaces
domains.question: Do ESP32, Pixoo, Timebox, iDotMatrix, ADB and mDNS paths discover, flash and render correctly?

domains.name: Voice
domains.question: Are push-to-talk, transcription and spoken replies routed to the right session and device?

domains.name: Stream Deck & Ulanzi plugins
domains.question: Do the deck plugins connect, recover, lay out keys and encoders, and dispatch host controls per platform?

domains.name: Terminal dashboard
domains.question: Does the TUI dashboard render sessions and the terrarium stably?

domains.name: Release & repository policy
domains.question: Do versions, release notes, runtime support and palette ratchets hold?
